summary: Label, control and message, wired together. The wrapper every form control belongs in.

pairs.dont: Lay out a label, an input and a hint by hand.
pairs.why: Hand-laid fields are where htmlFor, aria-describedby and aria-invalid go missing — they are invisible when they are wrong, so nothing catches it. Field generates the ids and hangs the wiring off them.

pairs.dont: Set invalid without rendering a FieldError.
pairs.do: Pair every invalid state with a message that says what to do.
pairs.why: Invalid with no error leaves a red border and nothing else — and because the hint is swapped out, the field says less than it did when it was valid.

pairs.dont: Try to show the hint and the error at once.
pairs.do: Let the error replace the hint, and repeat any format detail the error needs.
pairs.why: A screen reader announcing a format hint and a failure together is noisier than announcing the failure. If the format still matters, say it in the error: "MOS is measured to one decimal. Use 3.6."

pairs.dont: Mark required with an asterisk alone.
pairs.do: Pass required to FieldLabel and FieldControl together.
pairs.why: The asterisk is aria-hidden, because a screen reader reading "star" is not information. aria-required is what carries the fact; the asterisk is its visual half.

pairs.dont: Asterisk every field in a form where all of them are required.
pairs.do: Mark whichever set is smaller — required, or optional.
pairs.why: A column of asterisks carries no information. If only two fields of twelve are optional, label those two.

pairs.dont: Use the hint to warn — "Don't use spaces".
pairs.do: Use it to describe the expected shape — "Letters, digits and hyphens".
pairs.why: A hint written as a prohibition reads as an error that has already happened, so people check whether they have done something wrong before they have typed anything.

pairs.dont: Disable the control and leave the label at full strength.
pairs.why: A live-looking label above a dead control reads as a bug. Field dims the label and hint with the control, in one place.

a11y: The label is a real <label htmlFor>, so clicking it focuses the control and the hit target includes the text.
FieldError carries role="alert", so the failure is announced when it appears rather than when focus happens to reach the control.
aria-describedby points at the hint while valid and at the error while invalid — never at both, and never at a node that is not rendered.
The required asterisk is aria-hidden; aria-required on the control is what assistive tech reads.
